correctness.rationale: The ground vertices are the 21 unordered pairs, and a facet contains its center pair as well as the ten pairs disjoint from it. Independent enumeration agreed with the containment predicate on all 2,097,151 nonempty masks, producing 37,527 faces. The independent replay found 18,633 disjoint matches and sorted the entire directed Hasse graph (218,673 arrows), leaving one critical vertex and 260 critical 3-cells. The resulting CW model is a wedge of 260 three-spheres, regardless of the auxiliary mod-two check. For a permutation g the trace on H3 is 1-L(g). A nonempty invariant face consisting of r vertex cycles contributes (-1)^(r+1) to L, so it contributes (-1)^r to 1-L, where the empty face supplies +1. This clarifies the convention in the orbit-sum paragraph. The two independent trace formulas agree in all 15 classes. Exact irreducible character inner products reproduce all nine listed Specht types, with multiplicity two precisely for (4,2,1) and (3,2,1,1); their dimensions sum to 260. Rational Specht modules realize the absolutely irreducible characters, so this determines the rational module. The computation does not infer an equivariant CW model or integral Specht splitting.

value.rationale: This is a complete homotopy and symmetry calculation for a canonical distance-based complex on the next pair-Kneser graph after the known six-point case. The substantial difference from the open calculation and the appearance of two genuine repeated Specht types explain why the exact closed invariant matters. It gives a useful benchmark for a general formula or a persistence computation, without claiming either.
residual_risks: One graph and one radius; no claim about the persistence maps or the rest of the Kneser family.
